title: Electrical Wiring — Segregation of the Door Warning Channels in the Forward Fuselage

ata.title: Forward Fuselage Wiring — Door Warning Wiring

abstract: Re-routing of the two cargo door warning channels so that they share no bundle, clamp or connector shell in the forward fuselage, restoring the independence that the duplicated latch sensing standard assumes.

sections.planning_reason: When the second latch position sensor was introduced, both sensing channels of each cargo door station were carried in the same harness bundle for part of their run through the forward fuselage. A chafe finding on one aircraft exposed conductors from both channels at the same clamp position, which would have removed the whole benefit of the duplication had it progressed. A segregation review then found five further positions where the two channels share a bundle, a support or a connector shell.
sections.description: The second channel is re-routed on the opposite side of the frame using a new avionics bay cable assembly D9221113867714, and a splice module D9221004365569 is added at the transition into the avionics bay so that the second channel can be broken out without disturbing the first. Connector HOL285457-83 replaces the shared shell at the forward fuselage transition and grommets EN491538-6A protect the new penetrations. Plain washers AGS573791-88 are used at the bonding points. The circuit breaker at FIN 4387VC is re-allocated to the second channel.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Put the aircraft in the electrical safety condition for wiring work and remove power from the door warning system. Remove the forward cargo compartment lining panels and open the avionics bay racks. Identify and tag both door warning channels at every shared position listed in the accomplishment instructions. Remove the second channel conductors from the shared bundle, working from the door station towards the avionics bay. Install the new cable assembly D9221113867714 on the opposite side of the frame, using the new supports and fitting grommets EN491538-6A at every penetration. Install the splice module D9221004365569 at the avionics bay transition and terminate the second channel on it. Install the connector HOL285457-83 at the forward fuselage transition and re-terminate both channels on separate shells. Re-allocate the circuit breaker at FIN 4387VC and update the breaker panel legend. Bond the new supports using plain washers AGS573791-88 and measure the bonding resistance. Do a continuity and insulation check on both channels and confirm that they are electrically independent. Refit the lining panels and the racks. Do the door warning harness check of AMM-T-92-21-13-200-002-A and the cargo door operational test. Record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to TITAN-88 aircraft up to and including MSN T00190 that already carry the duplicated latch sensing standard, whether from production or from the retrofit Service Bulletin. Accomplishment on an aircraft still at the single sensor standard is not permitted, because the second channel does not yet exist. Aircraft from MSN T00193 onwards were built segregated.
sections.material_note: Kit K9221-1004-01 covers one aircraft. Kit lead time is eighteen weeks. The aircraft must not be released to service part-way through this Service Bulletin, since the intermediate state leaves both channels partially disconnected.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled base maintenance visit after the duplicated latch sensing standard is embodied, or within 48 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.
